comparisons.peer_topic: Private equity fund strategy and liquidity
comparisons.peer_summary: Private equity funds invest globally in industries via buyouts, recapitalizations, and distressed investments; as closed-end funds, their investments are generally not eligible for redemption, with uncertain timing for distributions upon liquidation.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs (GS) and Morgan Stanley (MS) disclose that their private equity and real estate fund investments are structured as closed-end funds, meaning they are generally not redeemable. Consequently, investors (the firms) only receive distributions upon the liquidation or monetization of the underlying assets, with the timing of such events being uncertain. GS explicitly states the timing is uncertain, while MS notes distributions are received as underlying investments are disposed and monetized.

sentences.text: Investments in Private Equity and Other funds and Real Estate funds generally are not redeemable due to the closed-end nature of these funds.
Instead, distributions from each fund will be received as the underlying investments of the funds are disposed and monetized.
Substantially all private equity, credit and real estate funds are closed-end funds in which the firm's investments are generally not eligible for redemption.
Distributions will be received from these funds as the underlying assets are liquidated or distributed, the timing of which is uncertain.

comparisons.peer_summary: Equity securities at fair value includes investments in private equity, real estate and hedge funds that are measured at net asset value (NAV).
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and GS measure their investments in private equity and real estate funds based on Net Asset Value (NAV). MS confirms this measurement applies regardless of whether the funds are accounted for under the equity method or fair value, while GS includes private equity and real estate funds within its equity securities measured at fair value using NAV.

sentences.text: The carrying amounts are measured based on the NAV of the fund taking into account the distribution terms applicable to the interest held.
This same measurement applies whether the fund investments are accounted for under the equity method or fair value.
• Equity securities, at fair value includes investments in private equity, real estate and hedge funds that are measured at NAV.

comparisons.peer_topic: Practical Expedient for Investments Measured at NAV
comparisons.peer_summary: Certain investments, including hedge funds, private equity, and real estate funds with fair values of $1.0 billion as of December 31, 2024 and 2023, are measured using net asset value per share as a practical expedient and are not required to be classified in the fair value hierarchy, primarily reported in other assets.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) disclose that investments in hedge funds, private equity, and real estate funds are measured using Net Asset Value (NAV) as a practical expedient for fair value estimation. MS specifies this applies to private equity, private credit, and other funds, while JPM notes these investments are excluded from the fair value hierarchy due to this measurement method.
